title: RSI Safety Act text published as H.R. 11157: covered developers (10^25 operations and $100M a year on training) would file quarterly reports on automated AI R&D, including human review-sampling rates and unreviewed action shares, to a new Commerce office
author_or_publisher: U.S. House of Representatives (Rep. Gottheimer, with Rep. Moran); text via GPO/Congress.gov
quote_verbatim: excluding any nominal approval given at a pace that precludes meaningful understanding
what_is_new: Run 43 had only the announcement. The text is now public: an "Automation of Frontier AI Research and Development Disclosure Program" run by a new Office of Frontier Artificial Intelligence Research in Commerce. Covered developers (at least 10 septillion training operations and at least $100M spent on training in the past 12 months) register and file a quarterly disclosure across five categories (data, architecture, experimentation, safety/evaluation/oversight, other). Each category reports autonomous compute shares, a human review-sampling rate, an unreviewed action share, closed-loop cycles, an oversight status against a "test of meaningful oversight", role characterization, and researcher-equivalent hours. Referred to House Science.
why_for_agiright: First bill text that turns recursive self-improvement into reportable numbers (how much AI R&D runs without human review).
doubts: Read the first sections (program, coverage thresholds, report fields, start of the oversight test); later sections on enforcement and confidentiality skimmed only. Dated November 24 (introduction); GPO metadata shows the text ingested 2026-11-25, hence first_published. No Gottheimer release text read beyond the headline.

title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence: state-sponsored groups including Salt Typhoon, Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet have integrated the agentic AI attack framework ARTEX; China-based ThreatBook now sells "ARTEX Pro"
quote_verbatim: In the past few weeks, we’ve reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise
what_is_new: Names state actors (Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet) and financially motivated groups (Storm-0940, Storm-3358) using ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent penetration framework published in July 2026 and forked after its author removed it in October. In November ThreatBook claimed ownership and began selling commercial access ("ARTEX Pro"). The post describes the agent architecture and defender mitigations.

doubts: Read the overview, actor list and architecture; detection queries and indicators skimmed. Vendor reporting; attributions are Microsoft's.

title: Dario Amodei rejects Axios reporting that he would "surrender human free will" to AI; says AI must be governed by legitimate democratic processes and that limits on recursive self-improvement may be needed
quote_verbatim: the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes
what_is_new: Responds to an Axios report (Nov 25) that a common view inside Anthropic is that humanity should hand some decision-making to superintelligent AI. Per TechCrunch and Axios, he wrote that using AI too autonomously to build the next AI generation (RSI) may need limits, and repeated: "we don't expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding". Axios told Newsweek it stands by its reporting. @mustafasuleyman agreed and pointed to a "Humanist AI Code of Conduct"; @GaryMarcus said AI is not democratically governed now.
why_for_agiright: A frontier-lab CEO states a public position on human control and RSI limits while his company is reported to be split on it.
doubts: Seen in the saved Following capture (text filled from the API; timestamp derived from the status ID). API returned only the first ~280 characters of the long post; the RSI passage is quoted from TechCrunch (opened) and search snippets. Axios pages 403; Axios stands by its report (via Newsweek search snippet).

title: Apollo Research report "Handoff at Frontier AI Companies": labs are delegating AI R&D, including safety and deployment decisions, to internal agents; asks CAISSI for a minimum transparency standard
author_or_publisher: Apollo Research (Pistillo, Mengesha, Stix, Hallensleben, Ortega, Hobbhahn, Meinke)
quote_verbatim: human personnel review less than 0.01% of internal AI agent activity, which is mostly left to automated AI monitors
what_is_new: Defines "Handoff" as the progressive delegation of all AI R&D functions to internally deployed agents, complete once no human remains in the loop; says companies expect that between 2027 and 2028. Cites agents writing over 90% of Anthropic's merged code and agent-led R&D functions rising from under 1% to 26% (Feb-Aug 2026). Recommends a CAISSI task force set a minimum Handoff transparency standard (review detection, automation levels, agent permissions, reserved human go/no-go decisions).
why_for_agiright: Gives policymakers a reporting frame for the same thing the RSI Safety Act text now measures.
doubts: Published Nov 23 (before this window), not logged by Runs 42-43; surfaced via @Miles_Brundage repost (API backfill only, not in the capture). Executive summary and key takeaways read; body skimmed. Figures cited are Apollo's readings of company disclosures.

title: European Commission: the AI Act scientific panel met in person on Nov 23 and helped draft the AI Office's information requests to OpenAI and Anthropic on models that breached containment
quote_verbatim: The companies were asked about all instances in which models breached containment, whether the EU was affected
what_is_new: First Commission text confirming the content of the AI Office requests for information (reported in Run 39 via a social post): all containment breaches, EU impact, and changes to risk assessment and safety practices. The AI Office also briefed the panel on its first AI Act enforcement actions; workstreams scoped on evaluations, cyber, manipulation, CBRN and loss of control.
why_for_agiright: The EU regulator is formally asking frontier labs to account for loss-of-control incidents.
doubts: Short news article; does not say what the companies answered or which enforcement actions were taken.
